  - **Page side** (`engineHarness.ts`): `BoundaryOutcome { ok; error? }` at 22–25. `window.runBoundary(name)` at 216–232 spawns `new Worker(new URL('./boundary.worker.ts', import.meta.url), {type:'module'})`, posts `{ name }` and resolves with the reply.
  - **Spec** (`engine.spec.ts` 135–139, helper 172–177):
    ```ts
    test('the u64 event boundary round-trips a bigint ...', async ({ page }) => {
      const outcome = await runBoundary(page, 'bigint');
      expect(outcome.error ?? '', 'bigint boundary failure').toBe('');
      expect(outcome.ok).toBe(true);
    });
    ```
  - **To add a fingerprint check:** add `case 'identityFingerprint'` to the worker. Either call the new function and throw on mismatch with the KAT string, or extend `BoundaryOutcome` with `value?: string` and assert `expect(outcome.value).toBe('<KAT>')` in the spec.
  - **Alternative that exercises the full path:** `engine.worker.ts` imports `* as glue` into `EngineHost` (lines 9–10, 20–21), so a facade-read test could go through `runRealEngine` instead.
- **Rust side:** the wasm-bindgen-test suite is `crates/wasm/tests/boundary.rs`, and it can use `cipherbox-core`. The Rust KAT itself belongs in `crates/core`.

**5. Build and typings**
- **Browser suite:** `packages/client/test/browser/build-wasm.mjs` runs `cargo build -p cipherbox-wasm --features conformance --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (debug), then `wasm-bindgen --target web --out-dir test/browser/pkg --out-name cipherbox_wasm`. Typings land in `packages/client/test/browser/pkg/cipherbox_wasm.d.ts`, and `tsconfig.browser-test.json` typechecks the harness against it. It's run by `apps/web` `build:wasm` / `dev` / `build`. Not wasm-pack.
- **`packages/client/src`** never sees the generated `.d.ts`. The new function must be added by hand to `EngineWasm` in `engineWasm.ts`.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

- **Link fields on a personal entry:** the codec refuses all three link fields on a personal entry, not only the deadline. CONTEXT.md says they belong only on a link entry.
- **Zero values:** a zero deadline is refused with the existing check `invalid-expiry`, which moves from the row to the entry. A cap of zero is accepted.

- **Retired `expiresAt`:** a row that still carries the key keeps it as a preserved unknown field. Its bytes and signature do not change. The old accept vector for that row is unchanged. The row zero-expiry reject vector is removed, because the key is no longer a field.

**Engine changes (kept to the minimum):**
- `entry_is_live` and the published-deadline check in conversion are removed. The owner-local invite record still holds the deadline that conversion checks.
- The reseal now carries `via_link` and `grantee_name` unchanged, so that a named row keeps a valid signature.
- The tests that asserted the row deadline are removed or rewritten.

- The write-wave re-mint does not carry the new link fields on the commitment entry or on the row. The brief assigns that re-map to a later slice. At present no code creates a link entry or a named row.

- I did not run the `/simplify`, `/security-review` and `/crypto-privacy-review` passes. The brief leaves reviews to a separate reviewer.

The worktree and the branch are unchanged for the reviewer.</result>

<result>None of the five candidates costs anything material. Each is small allocation or branch work on a path already dominated by an ECDSA verify, an HPKE seal or a worker round trip. I did find one material problem next to the re-seal candidate, but it is a size-budget problem, not an efficiency one. I checked every item below against the source in the worktree.

## Material (outside the efficiency angle)

**`crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal.rs:1056` with `crates/engine/src/content/limits.rs:42`: the re-seal now carries grantee names that its size budget never counted.**
- **What happens:** `reseal_scope_root` drops each row's unknown map so that the section size depends only on the grant count (see the comment at reseal.rs:1040-1044). The new code carries `via_link` and `grantee_name` forward instead.
- **Why it is unbudgeted:** `LEDGER_ROW_WIRE_BYTES = 224`, and its doc still describes the row as "an optional deadline, and framing". The new fields add up to about 331 bytes per row: `viaLink` about 42, `granteeName` about 269 at the 255-byte limit, and `nameSource` about 20.
- **Size of the gap:** at 1024 rows that is about 339 KB that nothing budgets for. `SECTION_FRAMING_SLACK_BYTES` is 64 KB.
- **Who can trigger it:** re-seal never checks the owner signature on a row. `enforce_committed_ledger` compares only `(tag, permission)`. So a committed write grantee can put a 255-byte name on every row.
- **Result:** the section then fails `resealable_section_bytes` at reseal.rs:1102 with `SectionNotResealable`. That is the "rotation-proof scope" outcome limits.rs:95-99 warns about.
- **Efficiency side effect:** the refusal comes only after every blob has been HPKE-sealed and the body AEAD-sealed. All of that work is wasted.
- **Possible fixes:** raise `LEDGER_ROW_WIRE_BYTES` to cover the full row, or carry a name only when `row_is_owner_attested` passes.
- **Confidence:** the byte counts are my own det-CBOR estimates. A 1024-row test with a maximum-length name on every row would confirm it.

## Candidates you named (all negligible)

1. **`crates/core/src/suite/contact.rs:173-183`, `identity_fingerprint` makes four heap allocations for a 24-character output.**
   - **Cost:** four small allocations: the transcript `Vec`, the hex `String`, the `Vec<&str>`, and the `join` result.
   - **Cheaper version:** feed `blake3::Hasher::new().update(FINGERPRINT_DOMAIN.as_bytes()).update(&sec1)` and finalize, with no transcript `Vec`. Then write straight into `String::with_capacity(24)`, adding a space after every fourth hex character. That is one allocation.
   - **Why it does not matter:** it is a user-triggered UI read. `fingerprint_identity_key` (engine `grants/contact.rs:76`) first decompresses the point in `from_sec1`, which is a modular square root and costs microseconds. The facade call then costs a worker `postMessage` round trip. Both dwarf the allocations.
   - **Design note:** the facade takes one key per round trip (`facade.ts:192`). A list of N grantees means N round trips. Nothing in `apps/` calls it yet. If a list view ever does, computing fingerprints in the engine's grant projection would remove those round trips.

2. **`crates/core/src/seal/grant.rs:988` and `:1117`: `GrantSetEntry::validate` runs twice when a commitment is decoded and then verified.**
   - **Where:** `from_value` calls it at decode. `verify_grant_set` (line 1161) then re-encodes through `encode_grant_set_commitment`, which calls it again for each entry.
   - **Cost:** one enum match plus three `Option` checks per entry, at most 1024 entries. That is nanoseconds.
   - **Why it does not matter:** the same verify also re-encodes the whole commitment and runs an ECDSA verify.
   - **Cheaper version:** fold the validate loop into the `assert_unknown_disjoint` loop at line 1124. That would change which error wins when an entry breaks two rules. The encoder deliberately checks in the decoder's order so both sides return the same error, so leave it as is.

3. **`crates/core/src/seal/write_body.rs:272`, `insert_optional_signed` clones the name (at most 255 bytes) into an owned `Value::Text`.**
   - **Cost:** one copy of at most 255 bytes each time a row is encoded or its recipient binding is encoded. The binding is encoded at sign, at verify (`row_is_owner_attested` in `facade.rs:4208` and `net/rotation.rs:4289`), and at `encode_write_body`.
   - **Why it cannot be avoided cheaply:** the codec's `Map` owns its keys and values. Every neighbouring field already does the same with `.to_vec()`, and `Map::insert` allocates each key. Removing the copy would need a borrowed or `Cow` value type in the codec, which is out of scope.
   - **Why it does not matter:** each binding encode is followed by an ECDSA verify, which costs far more.

4. **`crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal.rs:1056`, the re-seal clones `grantee_name` for every row.**
   - **Cost:** at most 1024 × 255 bytes, about 261 KB of allocation and copy. `encode_write_body` → `to_value` then copies each name a second time.
   - **Why it is needed:** `committed.grant_ledger` is borrowed (`&'a [GrantLedgerEntry]`, line 241), and `WriteBody` owns its rows.
   - **Cheaper version:** a write-body encoder that takes borrowed rows and skips `unknown`. The rows are rebuilt only to drop that map.
   - **Why it does not matter:** the same re-seal performs up to 1024 X25519/HPKE seals and an AEAD over a body of up to about 2 MB.

5. **`crates/core/src/seal/write_body.rs:136-139`, `GranteeName::new` scans characters after the byte-length check.**
   - **Cost:** the byte-length check runs first and short-circuits, so the `chars()` scan covers at most 255 bytes.
   - **Why a byte scan is not a drop-in:** `char::is_control` also matches C1 controls U+0080–U+009F. Those encode as the two bytes `0xC2 0x80`–`0x9F`, so checking single bytes for `< 0x20 || == 0x7F` would let them through. Keep the current form.

## One small extra (negligible)

**`crates/core/src/seal/write_body.rs:236-239`: the decoder copies the name before checking it.**
- **What happens:** `name.as_text()?.to_owned()` runs before `NameSource::from_value` and before the length check in `GranteeName::new`.
- **Cost:** on a hostile record, one extra copy of a name up to the write-body limit (about 2 MB) on a path that rejects anyway.
- **Cheaper version:** check the source and the length on the borrowed `&str` first, then call `to_owned`. For example, add a `GranteeName::check(&str)` that both `new` and the decoder use.
- **Why it does not matter:** it happens only on records that are rejected anyway, and the copy is bounded.</result>

## Findings

**A. `crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs:4300-4321` (candidate 7). The re-mint silently removes the new fields from both the commitment entry and the ledger row.**
- **What happens:** `mint_grant_row` builds the new entry with `GrantSetEntry::new`, which always makes a personal entry. The loop then copies only `unknown` back from `committed_entry` (line 4319). A committed link entry therefore comes out as a personal entry, without its `deadline`, `conversionPermission` or `admissionCap`. The owner then re-signs that weaker entry.
- **The row side:** the ledger row loses `via_link` and `grantee_name`.
- **Cost:**

  - `via_link` is gone, so admission counting (ADR 0023 D9) restarts at zero.

# Review of PR #1982 — `fix/1959-publish-above-observed-sequence` (head `4c016f7e1`)

Local verification in my worktree: `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p cipherbox-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; the four new tests pass. Against `main`'s source with the PR's tests kept, the `net.rs` test and two drain tests fail; `a_sibling_root_at_the_same_sequence_is_a_lost_race_the_next_pass_heals` passes either way (the PR body does not claim otherwise). Tree restored; no repository edit remains. Scratch artifacts: `~/.claude/scratch/w1963/C/review/{pr.diff,simplify.patch,test.log,clippy.log,without-fix*.log}`.

## Findings

### F1 — should-fix — CONFIRMED — `crates/engine/src/net/publish.rs:383-391`, `crates/engine/src/net/fanout.rs:250-256`

Defect: the confirm compares only the single freshest record the fan-out picks, and the fan-out keeps the FIRST endpoint on a sequence tie, so a same-sequence sibling on a later endpoint reads as `Published`.
Failure scenario: A and B both mint N+1. If A's bytes sit on endpoint 0 (or endpoint 0 is transiently `Err` for A at confirm time), A reads its own bytes back: `Published`. B reads its own bytes from its first endpoint: `Published`. Both self-adopt N+1 and dequeue. The split is never healed; the next resolve on either device takes the other's N+1 as `Current` by sequence alone (`resolve.rs:357`), so one create is silently lost. The issue's "Expected" says the read-back must classify a same-sequence different-bytes record as a lost race; the PR meets that for one endpoint order only, and `net.rs` tests only that order.
Fix: let the confirm see every endpoint answer. Smallest form: in `fanout_get_under` track `contested: bool` (a verified record at the best sequence with different bytes was seen) and expose it through a confirm-only `fanout_get_contested(...) -> Option<(VerifiedRecord, Vec<u8>, bool)>`; then in `publish.rs`:

```rust
Some((_, bytes, contested)) if bytes == record_bytes && !contested => PublishOutcome::Published { sequence },
Some((observed, _, _)) if observed.sequence >= sequence => PublishOutcome::LostRace { .. },
```

Add `publish_confirm_reads_a_sibling_on_a_later_endpoint_as_a_lost_race` (mirror of the new `net.rs` test, sibling seeded on endpoint 1 only). Both racing devices then halt, the next read leg adopts the tie winner, and each rebases and signs above.

### F2 — should-fix — CONFIRMED — `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:5753`

Defect: the pre-signature re-resolve runs only for the scope root; interior folders share the same name derivation (`write_name` drain.rs:794, `write_name_signer` session.rs:205) and the same stale-base window.
Failure scenario: `ensure_folder` loads an interior folder once per pass and returns early on `pass.holds(folder)` (drain.rs:2397); uploads run between that load and the signature. Device B loads F at n and uploads for minutes; device A creates a child in F and confirms F at n+1; B signs n+1 over a body without A's child. Under F1's endpoint order B's confirm is `Published` and A's create is lost with no error. The issue's "Expected" is written for "a publish", not only a root.
Fix: generalise `reresolve_scope_root` to `reresolve_before_signing(plane, folder, built_on)`: root uses `root_adopter`; an interior folder builds the `ChildAdopter` exactly as `load_child_node` does (drain.rs:2305-2313) and runs the same `resolve_gated(NoCache)` / `TrustViolation` / `> built_on` logic. Drop the `if is_scope_root` guard. Add a `write_plane` test with two devices writing one interior folder mid-pass. If the orchestrator keeps the PR root-scoped, file the interior case as a follow-up with a dependency edge before merge; the blueprint sweep needs only the root.

### F3 — should-fix — CONFIRMED — `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:5814` and the `Halt::Attempt` doc `:391-397`

Defect: a pre-signature lost race is charged against `ATTEMPT_BUDGET` (5, then `AttemptsExhausted` dead-letter, drain.rs:1918-1935), but the budget's own rule (`:571-575`, "spent only by a halt the valve could attribute to these bytes") and the `Attempt` doc's reason ("a retry re-signs at the same sequence") do not hold here: nothing was PUT, the adopt raised the floor, the retry signs higher.
Failure scenario: device A drains a batch of creates (one root publish per create); device B has a create with a long upload at its head. Each B pass re-resolves after its upload, sees A's newer root, halts `Attempt`. Charges are durable and never decay while the op stays queued. After five losses B's create is dead-lettered although it was never refused. Four independent reads (altitude, crypto, spec, standards) reached the same conclusion.
Fix: charge it to the unattributed budget — return `Halt::Unclassified` at drain.rs:5814 with a one-line reason, or add `Halt::LostRace` handled next to `Unclassified` in `apply_valve` (charge_unattributed, no name handed back, same `upload_failure` text as `Attempt`). Restore the original `Attempt` doc. Add a test asserting the attempt count stays 0 after a pre-signature lost race.

### F4 — should-fix — CONFIRMED — `blueprint/engine.md:927-930`

Defect: "…the two-device publish fix — re-resolve, then sign above the highest sequence seen — which is not landed; without it two owner devices … publish two records at one sequence." This PR lands that fix for the scope root the sweep writes. The clause is a status marker in the exact form AGENTS.md "Tracker references" prescribes, and that rule says it "stops being true in the same diff that falsifies it". No design statement changes, so no ADR is needed.
Fix (in this PR): keep the dependency, drop the status clause: "The sweep depends on the two-device publish fix — the drain re-resolves the root through the gate just before it signs and signs above the highest sequence it observed, and a confirm that reads a sibling's record at its own sequence is a lost race the next pass rebases and signs above."

### F5 — nit — simplify patch at `~/.claude/scratch/w1963/C/review/simplify.patch` (110 lines; builds, tests green, clippy clean; tree restored)

Hunks: (a) `drain.rs` — extract `gated_scope_root(scope, end, mode) -> Result<GatedResolve, Halt>`; `resolve_scope_root` and `reresolve_scope_root` both call it; the redundant `name` parameter is removed (`end.root_name` is the same value, drain.rs:2220); (b) `reresolve_scope_root` doc cut to five lines with the blueprint citation, no happy-path narration; (c) `publish.rs:380-382` confirm comment cut to one sentence. Not applied (author's call): `write_plane.rs` `root_sequence` duplicates `sequence_at` (11 callers, so I did not widen it); the endpoint assert loop is copied four times; the `net.rs` and `write_plane.rs` docs re-derive the two-device rule that `LostRace` already states; "the CAS law" is not a CONTEXT.md term — cite blueprint/engine.md "Publish".

### F6 — nit — CONFIRMED — `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:5799-5809` (cost)

Every root publish adds one sequential fan-out GET (E endpoints) plus, on the usual equal-floor `Current` path, a gateway head-block fetch and unseal (`adopter.rs` `recover_own_scope_material` → `fetch_head_block`; the fresh `root_adopter` holds no local head). Per pass: r × (E + 1) extra round trips for r root-level ops. Rule 6 forbids skipping the gate; the only safe saving is handing the pass's held head block to the adopter as `local`. Optional.

### Residuals outside the diff (follow-ups, not blockers)

- `resolve.rs:357`: a record at exactly the floor is `Current` by sequence alone; a sibling's different bytes at the floor are never a conflict. Deepest home of the single-writer assumption (store the floor record hash beside the floor).
- `publish.rs:332`: `floor + 1` is unchecked; a key-holding sibling at `u64::MAX` wraps the mint to 0 in release. Use `checked_add`.

## PR body and title

Title: parentheses only in the scope. Body: bare `Closes #1959.`, no attribution, "fails without the fix" claims verified true. One overstatement: "reads another record at our own sequence as `LostRace`" holds only when the fan-out picks the sibling's record (F1).

## Gate verdicts

- `/simplify`: 3 source cleanups applied, captured as a patch (F5), tree clean.
- `/security-review`: no high-confidence vulnerability; every attack path examined is closed (gate fail-closed, floors move only on a gate pass, the sequence is inside the signed bytes, no clock or RNG, `Zeroizing` fields dropped by their terminal owner).
- `/crypto-privacy-review`: risk LOW for the diff; MEDIUM residual design gap (F1, F2); no crypto, KDF, zeroization, or test-secret issue.
- `/code-review` Standards: 2 HARD comment-rule breaches (the `Attempt` doc, the re-derived rule — covered by F3/F5), the rest judgement-call duplication (F5). Spec: 2 partial requirements (F1, F2), no scope creep, blueprint status clause must change (F4).</result>

input.message:
The reviewer of PR 1982 confirmed the findings below. Apply all of them, commit, and make ONE push. Then wait for CI green with one polling script and report. Do not mark the PR ready and do not request a review. The reviewer's artifacts are under `~/.claude/scratch/w1963/C/review/` (read `simplify.patch` and `pr.diff`).

F1 (should-fix) `crates/engine/src/net/publish.rs:383-391`, `crates/engine/src/net/fanout.rs:250-256`: the confirm compares only the freshest record the fan-out picks, and the fan-out keeps the FIRST endpoint on a sequence tie. So a same-sequence sibling on a later endpoint reads as `Published`, both devices self-adopt N+1, and one create is lost. Fix: let the confirm see every endpoint answer. In `fanout_get_under` track `contested: bool` (a verified record at the best sequence with different bytes was seen) and expose it through a confirm-only variant that returns `(VerifiedRecord, bytes, contested)`. In `publish.rs`: `Published` only when bytes match AND not contested; otherwise when the observed sequence is >= ours, `LostRace`. Add the test `publish_confirm_reads_a_sibling_on_a_later_endpoint_as_a_lost_race` (the sibling seeded on endpoint 1 only).

F2 (should-fix) `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:5753`: the pre-signature re-resolve runs only for the scope root, but interior folders share the same name derivation and the same stale-base window (`ensure_folder` loads once per pass, uploads run between the load and the sign). Fix: generalise `reresolve_scope_root` to `reresolve_before_signing(plane, folder, built_on)`: the root uses `root_adopter`; an interior folder builds the `ChildAdopter` exactly as `load_child_node` does (drain.rs:2305-2313) and runs the same `resolve_gated(NoCache)` / `TrustViolation` / `> built_on` logic. Drop the `if is_scope_root` guard. Add a `write_plane` test with two devices that write one interior folder mid-pass.

F3 (should-fix) `drain.rs:5814` and the `Halt::Attempt` doc at `:391-397`: a pre-signature lost race must not spend `ATTEMPT_BUDGET`; nothing was PUT, the adopt raised the floor, the retry signs higher. After five losses a valid create is dead-lettered. Fix: add `Halt::LostRace` handled next to `Unclassified` in `apply_valve` (charge_unattributed, no name handed back, the same `upload_failure` text as `Attempt`), or return `Halt::Unclassified` with a one-line reason. Restore the original `Attempt` doc. Add a test that asserts the attempt count stays 0 after a pre-signature lost race.

F4 (should-fix) `blueprint/engine.md:927-930`: the clause "which is not landed; without it two owner devices ... publish two records at one sequence" is a status marker that this PR falsifies. Replace the passage with: "The sweep depends on the two-device publish fix: the drain re-resolves the root through the gate just before it signs and signs above the highest sequence it observed, and a confirm that reads a sibling's record at its own sequence is a lost race the next pass rebases and signs above." Keep the dependency, drop the status clause. No ADR is needed because no design statement changes.

F5 (nit): apply `~/.claude/scratch/w1963/C/review/simplify.patch` (extract `gated_scope_root`, shorter docs, one-sentence confirm comment). Adjust it to F2. Also: replace the phrase "the CAS law" in test docs with a citation of blueprint/engine.md "Publish"; do not re-derive the two-device rule in the `net.rs` and `write_plane.rs` docs, `LostRace` states it once.

F6 (nit, optional): the fresh `root_adopter` fetches the head block again on every re-resolve. If the pass already holds the head block, hand it to the adopter as `local`. Do it if it is a small change; skip it and say so if not.

Residual (do it, trivial): `publish.rs:332` `floor + 1` is unchecked; use `checked_add` and fail closed on overflow.

Residual (do NOT build; tell me in your report whether it is small): `resolve.rs:357` treats a record at exactly the floor as `Current` by sequence alone, so a sibling's different bytes at the floor are never a conflict.

Run `cargo test -p cipherbox-engine`, `cargo test --workspace --exclude fuser`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy with `-D warnings`, the wasm32 check, `pnpm lint:tracker-refs`, and `pnpm lint:md` for the blueprint edit. Check `git log --format=%B origin/main..HEAD | grep -i "co-authored\|generated with"` prints nothing. Report the new head SHA and CI status.

<result>## SECURITY REVIEW COMPLETE

**Files analyzed:** 37 (diff) plus the source of every touched path
**Crypto operations touched:** ECDSA preimages (grant-set commitment, recipient binding), unkeyed BLAKE3 fingerprint, re-seal and re-mint producers
**Issues found:** 0 critical, 2 high, 1 medium, 2 low

### Findings

#### [HIGH] The write wave re-signs a committed link entry as a perpetual personal grant

**Location:** `crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs:4308-4321` (`remint_grants`), `crates/engine/src/grants/ledger.rs:156-192` (`mint_grant_row`)

`remint_grants` builds the re-minted entry with `mint_grant_row`, which calls `GrantSetEntry::new` (always `Personal`, no `deadline`, no `admission_cap`, no `conversion_permission`), then copies only `unknown` from `committed_entry`. The row comes from `mint_grant_row` too, so `via_link` and `grantee_name` are gone and the row is owner-signed without them.

Scenario: the decoder now accepts a link entry, so a record authored by the mint slice (or any newer build) holds `{kind: link, deadline, admissionCap}` at `read`. The owner revokes an unrelated write grantee, which runs a write wave. The wave re-mints the link entry as a personal `read` entry with no deadline and no cap, and the owner signs it. The link holder keeps reading past the deadline for ever, the cap is unenforceable, and every converted row loses the `viaLink` that ADR 0023 D9 counts. This is fail-open on the field this PR introduces, in a function this PR edits, so it belongs in this PR, not the rotation slice.

Fix: carry every owner-signed field by struct update, and re-sign the row with the carried fields:

```rust
let commitment_entry = GrantSetEntry {
    tag: minted.commitment_entry.tag,
    masked_recipient_enc_pk: minted.commitment_entry.masked_recipient_enc_pk,
    pseudonym_pk: minted.commitment_entry.pseudonym_pk,
    ..committed_entry.clone()   // kind, deadline, conversion_permission, admission_cap, unknown
};
let mut ledger_entry = minted.ledger_entry;
if row_is_owner_attested(&owner_identity, row, old_name) {
    ledger_entry.via_link = row.via_link.map(|t| new_tag_of[&t]);   // old tag -> re-minted tag (ADR 0023 D2)
    ledger_entry.grantee_name = row.grantee_name.clone();
    ledger_entry.owner_sig = sign_recipient_binding(self.owner, new_name, &ledger_entry).to_compact();
}
```

The old-to-new tag map is available from the same loop. An unattested row's name and via-link are a write grantee's to choose, so they follow `recipient_identity_pk` and drop.

#### [HIGH] The re-seal budget is sized for a 224-byte row and copies writer-authored names of up to 565 bytes

**Location:** `crates/engine/src/content/limits.rs:42`, `crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal.rs:836,1052-1058,1104`, `crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal/tests.rs:870-941`

A bare row measures 234 bytes on the wire (`a5` map, keys, 64+32+33+32 bytes, `"read"`), already over `LEDGER_ROW_WIRE_BYTES = 224`. A row with `viaLink` + a 255-byte `granteeName` + `nameSource: "claimant"` measures 565. `reseal_scope_root` runs `enforce_committed_ledger` only (tag + permission, line 836) and then copies `via_link` and `grantee_name` from every committed row verbatim (1055-1056) with no `row_is_owner_attested` check. `resealable_section_bytes(1024)` = 909,312. Measured from the KAT vectors, a maximal bare re-seal is about 675 KB (read blob 281, row 234, child ref 98, history link 181 per item); full-width rows add 341 x 1024 = 349 KB, to about 1,024 KB, over the budget by about 115 KB. The break-even is about 750 committed rows.

Scenario: a committed write grantee on a scope with 750 or more committed grants re-authors the write body with a 255-byte name and `nameSource` on every row (no signature needed: the re-seal never checks one). The owner's next revoke hits `SectionNotResealable` (`reseal.rs:1104`), which `net/rotation.rs:3828` maps to `NotLanded`, on every retry. The scope is rotation-proof and the writer is un-revocable. The maximal test at `reseal/tests.rs:870` uses `attested_row` bare rows with a padded unknown map the re-seal drops, so it cannot see this.

Fix, both halves: (1) set `LEDGER_ROW_WIRE_BYTES` to the full-width row derived from the constants (`234 + 42 + (14 + MAX_GRANTEE_NAME_BYTES) + 20`, rounded to 576) so an honest owner with 1024 named grantees can still rotate; (2) carry `via_link` and `grantee_name` only when `row_is_owner_attested`, which removes the writer lever entirely. Rebuild the maximal test with full-width rows.

#### [MEDIUM] `GranteeName` admits bidi overrides and zero-width characters in an owner-signed name shown beside the fingerprint

**Location:** `crates/core/src/seal/write_body.rs:135-141`; engine law at `crates/engine/src/name.rs:92-105`

`char::is_control` covers Cc only. U+202E, U+2066-2069, U+200B, U+FEFF, U+2028 are Cf/Zl and pass. The engine already refuses exactly this set for node names (`validate_name`, `NameError::DeceptiveCharacter`) and strips it at render, but core cannot import that set, and the claim name will be validated by the codec every build shares.

Scenario: a claimant suggests `"Alice\u{202E}renwo"`. Conversion copies it into a row the owner signs with flag `claimant`; the people table and every co-writer render "Alice" with "owner" drawn reversed beside the fingerprint; a line separator (U+2028) fakes a second confirmation line, which is the exact case the control-character KAT vector says it closes.

Fix: move the `is_deceptive` character set into core (a small `crates/core/src/name.rs`, or beside `GranteeName`), have `GranteeName::new` refuse it with `invalid-grantee-name`, add a reject KAT vector, and have `crates/engine/src/name.rs` use the core set so the law has one home.

#### [LOW] A link entry needs no deadline and no admission cap

**Location:** `crates/core/src/seal/grant.rs:898-916` (`validate`)

`validate` refuses link fields on a personal entry and a non-`read` link, and nothing else. A `{kind: link}` entry with no `deadline` and no `admissionCap` encodes, signs and decodes. CONTEXT.md "Link entry" says it carries all three. Scenario: the conversion slice reads `admission_cap: None` as unlimited, which is the 1024-row enrolment ADR 0023 D9 exists to stop. Either require both on `Link` in `validate` (fail-closed, one more reject vector) or write the absent-cap rule now (absent = zero admissions).

#### [LOW] `expiresAt: 0` now decodes

The `ledger-zero-expiry` reject vector is gone; a row carrying `expiresAt: 0` decodes as a preserved unknown and re-encodes byte-stable. Acceptable under the retirement and no engine path reads it (checked below). Note only.

### Checklist verdicts

- **A. Preimage:** clean. `Map::insert` keeps canonical order (`value.rs:224`), keys are distinct, `granteeName` and `nameSource` always travel together, so the encoding is injective over the field set. The `read-grantee` and `write-grantee` preimages and signatures are byte-identical to `main` (checked with `git show main:...`). Removal of a present field fails with `identity-signature-invalid`, class `trust`, pinned by four reject vectors the manifest test asserts by check and class.
- **B. Commitment:** clean apart from the LOW above. `sign_grant_set`, `verify_grant_set`, `verify_grant_set_bound` and `encode_grant_section` (`section.rs:480`) all route through `encode_grant_set_commitment`, which runs `validate` on every entry; every engine producer calls `sign_grant_set`. `GRANT_SET_ENTRY_KNOWN` and `LEDGER_ENTRY_KNOWN` list the new keys and `assert_unknown_disjoint` (`body.rs:567`) is a release `Err`. Non-text `kind` fails `unexpected-type` through the guard's `?`; explicit `"personal"` fails `invalid-entry-kind`; `deadline: 0` fails `invalid-expiry` and `NonZeroU64` makes it unrepresentable on encode.
- **C. Fingerprint:** clean. It is a public digest, not a derivation: public input, public output, no secret, so it needs no catalog edge, which matches core.md line 88-90. Plain `blake3::hash` cannot collide with any `derive_key`/`keyed_hash` edge (BLAKE3 mode flags separate them); the only other plain-hash use is `H(ciphertext)` in `structure.rs`, whose digest no consumer ever compares with a fingerprint. `from_sec1` refuses any length but 33; output is 20 lowercase hex chars in five groups, 80 bits; domain and width are pinned in the manifest and the browser suite asserts the same two vector strings against the WASM export.
- **D. Retired `expiresAt`:** clean. `write_body_accept.json` shows six inserted lines only; `entry_is_live` is deleted; the only deadline reads left are `RecordedInvite::expires_at` (`invite.rs:909`) and view structs. `facade.rs:10640` is a device-approval row, not a ledger row.
- **E. Redaction and secrets:** clean. `GranteeName` Debug uses `RedactedText`, `via_link` uses `RedactedBytes`; test scalars are fixtures; the WASM error carries no bytes.
- **I. Determinism:** clean. No clock or RNG in the touched core paths; `now` stays injected in `convert_invite_claim`.
- **J. Gates:** clean. `encode_refusals.rs` runs under `--release` in job "Core KATs (native + WASM)" (and again in the plain and wasm32-wasip1 runs); `engine.spec.ts` runs in "Client Browser Suite". All assertions are behavioural.

### Additional test cases, prioritized

1. `reseal/tests.rs`: the maximal committed set with full-width rows (`via_link`, a 255-byte name, `nameSource`) re-seals inside `resealable_section_bytes(MAX_GRANT_BLOBS)`. Fails today.
2. `reseal/tests.rs`: a name and via-link on a row whose `owner_sig` does not verify are not carried by the re-seal.
3. `net/rotation.rs` tests: the re-mint carries a link entry's `kind`, `deadline`, `conversion_permission`, `admission_cap`, and `verify_grant_set` passes over the re-minted set.
4. `net/rotation.rs` tests: the re-mint re-maps an attested row's `via_link` to the link's new tag, carries the name, and the new row verifies under `new_name`; an unattested row's name drops with its identity key.
5. `encode_refusals.rs` (release): `GranteeName::new` refuses U+202E, U+2066, U+200B, U+FEFF, U+2028; `write_body_reject.json` gains one vector.
6. `grant.rs`: a link entry missing `deadline` or `admissionCap` is refused (or a test pinning that it is accepted, once the rule is written).
7. `grant_set_reject.json`: `kind: 1` and `deadline: "soon"` fail `unexpected-type`; `admissionCap: 0` on a link is accepted.
8. `write_body.rs`: a 253-byte ASCII name plus one 2-byte char (255 bytes) is accepted and 254 plus one 2-byte char (256) is refused, pinning the byte bound at a UTF-8 boundary.
9. `write_body.rs`: swapping the `granteeName` and `nameSource` values (`"owner"`/`Owner` vs `"Alice"`/`Claimant`) yields distinct preimages, pinning that both keys and both value types are in the signed map.
10. `kat_manifest.rs`: the browser suite's literal fingerprint vectors equal `fingerprint.json` (or read the JSON in `boundary.worker.ts`), so the two copies cannot drift apart.

### Recommendations

1. Fix the re-mint in this PR: struct-update the committed entry and re-sign carried row fields (finding 1).
2. Resize `LEDGER_ROW_WIRE_BYTES` to the full row and carry names only from attested rows; rebuild the maximal re-seal test with full-width rows (finding 2).
3. Move the deceptive-character set into core and refuse it in `GranteeName::new` with a KAT vector (finding 3).

Report location: inline. Scratch helper only: `/Users/myankelev/.claude/scratch/w1963/A/review/measure.py`.</result>

## Problem

A reader treats a record at exactly its epoch floor as `Current` by sequence alone (`crates/engine/src/net/resolve.rs`, the floor comparison in the resolve outcome). A sibling device's record with different bytes at the same sequence never reads as a conflict. The two-device publish fix makes the drain re-resolve and sign strictly above the highest sequence it observed, and makes a confirm that reads a sibling's record at its own sequence a lost race. A reader that later resolves the name at its floor still cannot tell the two records apart.

## Expected

The engine stores a hash of the floor record next to the floor. A resolve that reads a record at the floor sequence with a different hash reports a distinct outcome, and every consumer handles it: the tick root leg, the focus legs, the drain, rotation and the liveness hold. A cold cache has nothing to compare and keeps the present rule.

## Notes

Found by the review of the two-device publish fix. The fix needs a decision on what a reader does with a different record at exactly its floor: a trust violation or a new outcome. A new `ResolveOutcome` variant changes every consumer, so the change is not small.
EOF

greptile-apps crates/engine/src/net/publish.rs:389
 **First-endpoint tie remains split** When our record is on the first endpoint and a sibling's different record is on another endpoint at the same sequence, confirm reports `LostRace`. On retry, a normal resolve still selects our bytes, so the drain can treat the queued create as already satisfied and drop it without publishing a higher record. The other endpoint then keeps serving different contents at that sequence.

# Review of PR #1983 — feat(core): link fields, named ledger row, key fingerprint

Head `ae60628392c00fec9095090b9b69270c038ba2be`, branch `feat/1963-core-link-fields`. CI: every check green at head. PR body: no attribution, bare `Closes #N.` lines, title parentheses hold the scope only.

## Findings (by severity)

### should-fix 1 — the re-seal budget does not count the new row fields
- `crates/engine/src/content/limits.rs:42` (`LEDGER_ROW_WIRE_BYTES = 224`) with `crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal.rs:1055-1056`.
- Defect: `reseal_scope_root` now copies `via_link` and `grantee_name` from every committed row. The per-row budget still describes the old row. Measured from the KAT bytes: a bare row is 234 bytes, a linked row with a short name is 314-319 bytes, a row with a 255-byte name is about 565 bytes.
- Failure scenario: `enforce_committed_ledger` compares only `(tag, permission)`, and the re-seal never checks the row owner signature. A committed write grantee puts a 255-byte `granteeName` on every row. The minted section exceeds `resealable_section_bytes` (reseal.rs:1102) and the re-seal returns `SectionNotResealable`. The scope becomes rotation-proof. The maximal re-seal test (`reseal/tests.rs:874-941`) uses bare rows, so nothing catches it.
- Fix: derive the per-row budget from core constants (`234 + 42 + MAX_GRANTEE_NAME_BYTES + ~34`) with a compile-time assert, and extend the maximal re-seal test to rows with `via_link` and a 255-byte name. Alternative: carry `grantee_name` only when `row_is_owner_attested` passes.

### should-fix 2 — the write-wave re-mint drops every new owner-signed field
- `crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs:4313-4321` (`remint_grants`).
- Defect: the re-minted entry comes from `GrantSetEntry::new` (always `Personal`); only `unknown` is copied from `committed_entry`. `kind`, `deadline`, `conversion_permission`, `admission_cap` are lost and the owner re-signs a personal entry. The row loses `via_link` and `grantee_name`.
- Failure scenario: an owner device on this build re-mints a record that another build wrote with a link entry. The link loses its deadline and cap; its admitted rows lose the via-link reference. This fails open. No producer mints a link entry yet, but the decoder already accepts one.
- Spec note: #1965 defers only the via-link re-map; #1973 names only the re-map. The loss of the entry link fields and the grantee name is a silent gap.
- Fix: `GrantSetEntry { tag, masked_recipient_enc_pk, ..committed_entry.clone() }` (keep the pseudonym check) so every owner-signed field carries by default; carry `grantee_name` when `row_is_owner_attested` passes; until the tag re-map lands, carry `via_link` unchanged or return `Rejected` for a row that has one, and state the re-map in #1973.

### nit 3 — absence-justifying comment
- `crates/engine/src/grants/invite.rs:751-753`: "Nothing in a resolved record this build mints marks a row as an invite". This diff adds `EntryKind::Link` and `viaLink`; the sentence turns false when a link entry mints. input.message:
The reviewers of PR 1983 confirmed the findings below. Apply all of them, commit, and make ONE push. Then wait for CI green with one polling script and report. Do not mark the PR ready and do not request a review. Lane D builds on your branch (`feat/1963-engine-link-mint-read`, stacked on yours), so keep the wire names and public signatures you already exposed stable where you can, and list every renamed or re-typed public item in your report.

SHOULD-FIX 1: the write-wave re-mint drops every new owner-signed field. `crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs:4308-4321` `remint_grants` builds the entry with `mint_grant_row` → `GrantSetEntry::new` (always personal) and copies only `unknown`. Fix: build the re-minted entry by struct update so `kind`, `deadline`, `conversion_permission`, `admission_cap` and `unknown` carry from `committed_entry` (keep the pseudonym check). For the row: when `row_is_owner_attested` passes, carry `grantee_name` and the name source, re-map `via_link` from the old tag to the re-minted tag (the old-to-new tag map is available in the same loop), and re-sign the row with `sign_recipient_binding` under the new name. An unattested row's name and via-link drop with its identity key. Tests in `net/rotation.rs`: the re-mint carries a link entry's four fields and `verify_grant_set` passes over the re-minted set; the re-mint re-maps an attested row's `via_link` to the link's new tag, carries the name, and the new row verifies under the new name; an unattested row's name drops.

SHOULD-FIX 2: the re-seal budget is sized for a bare row. `crates/engine/src/content/limits.rs:42` `LEDGER_ROW_WIRE_BYTES = 224`, but a bare row measures 234 bytes on the wire and a row with `viaLink`, a 255-byte `granteeName` and `nameSource` measures about 565. `reseal_scope_root` (`rotation/reseal.rs:1052-1058`) copies `via_link` and `grantee_name` from every committed row with no owner-signature check, so a committed write grantee can put a 255-byte name on every row of a scope with about 750 grants and make every revoke fail with `SectionNotResealable`. Fix both halves: derive `LEDGER_ROW_WIRE_BYTES` from the constants (`234 + 42 + (14 + MAX_GRANTEE_NAME_BYTES) + 20`, rounded up to 576) with a test or const assert that pins the measured maximal row; and carry `via_link` and `grantee_name` only when `row_is_owner_attested` passes. Rebuild the maximal re-seal test (`rotation/reseal/tests.rs:870-941`) with full-width rows so it fits inside `resealable_section_bytes(MAX_GRANT_BLOBS)`; add a test that a name on a row whose owner signature does not verify is not carried.

SHOULD-FIX 3: `GranteeName::new` (`crates/core/src/seal/write_body.rs:135-141`) refuses only `char::is_control` (Cc). Bidi overrides and isolates (U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069), zero-width characters (U+200B-200D, U+2060, U+FEFF) and U+2028/2029 pass. The engine already refuses that set for node names in `crates/engine/src/name.rs:92-105` `is_deceptive`. Fix: move the deceptive-character set into core (a small module beside `GranteeName` or `crates/core/src/name.rs`), make `GranteeName::new` and the decoder refuse it with `invalid-grantee-name`, add a reject KAT vector, and make the engine `name.rs` use the core set so the law has one home. Add release-run cases in `encode_refusals.rs` for U+202E, U+2066, U+200B, U+FEFF, U+2028.

SHOULD-FIX 4: a `{kind: link}` entry with no `deadline` or no `admissionCap` encodes and decodes. Read CONTEXT.md "link entry" and ADR 0023 D9: require on a link entry every field CONTEXT.md says it carries, in `validate`, on decode and encode, with one reject vector per missing field and a release-run case. A cap of zero stays accepted.

NIT 5: absence-justifying comments. `crates/engine/src/grants/invite.rs:750-752` ("Nothing in a resolved record this build mints marks a row as an invite") and the same shape at `invite.rs:307`: replace with what the code does, for example "`links` is the owner's own record of the live links on this scope; a claim converts only against one of those." `crates/core/src/seal/write_body.rs:599-601` ("The decoder's grantee-name rejects need no guard here"): delete the sentence.

NIT 6: rationale restated three times: keep the CI-step comment in `.github/workflows/ci-rust.yml`; drop the copies in `crates/core/tests/encode_refusals.rs:1-3` and the `grant.rs` test doc.

NIT 7: terminology and types. Rename the check id `invalid-expiry` on the commitment entry to `invalid-deadline` (CONTEXT.md names the concept "deadline"; the ledger row check is retired). `invite.rs:356` hand-checks `deadline.0 == 0` on `UnixMillis` while core types the deadline as `NonZeroU64`; use the typed value. Rename the `seal` re-export `EntryKind` to `GrantSetEntryKind` if the rename is contained; skip it and say so if it spreads wide.

NIT 8: duplicates and dead code. `kat_gen.rs:7667-7680` `entry_with` has a dead `retain` loop (`Map::insert` replaces) and repeats `grant_set_entry_map`; `kat_gen.rs:5940` `named_entry` repeats `good_entry()`; `kat_gen.rs:5753` `named_ledger_row` repeats `signed_ledger_row`; `write_body.rs:1237` `named_row` repeats `signed_row`: share one sign step. `kat_manifest.rs:4440-4444` `binding_row` inlines the `"claimant"|"owner"` match a third time: add `NameSource::from_wire(&str) -> Option<Self>` and use it in `from_value` and the test; also replace the positional `binding_row(name, [&String; 3], [&Option<String>; 3], signature)` signature with the vector struct. `grant.rs:2270` and `write_body.rs:1389` repeat the tests in `tests/encode_refusals.rs`: keep only the release-run copies. `grant.rs:900` `GrantSetEntry::validate` is `pub` with no external caller: make it private. `packages/client/src/testkit.ts:532` `fingerprintKeys` is never read: delete. `invite.rs:1411` the `mint` closure repeats the `link()` helper at 1645: use the helper. `packages/client/test/browser/boundary.worker.ts:55-65` hand-copies `fingerprint.json`: import the vector file instead. `crates/engine/src/grants/contact.rs` test module: put the `use` lines before `#[test]`.

NIT 9: KAT coverage. Add one accept vector per link field on its own (not only the all-fields vector), reject vectors that pin `commitment-invalid` when `kind`, `conversionPermission` or `admissionCap` is edited after signing, a vector with `conversionPermission` on a personal entry, an unknown `kind`, `kind: 1` and `deadline: "soon"` as `unexpected-type`, `admissionCap: 0` on a link accepted. In `write_body.rs` unit tests: a 253-byte ASCII name plus one 2-byte char (255 bytes) accepted and 254 plus one 2-byte char (256) refused; swapping the `granteeName` and `nameSource` values yields distinct preimages.

Keep the explicit `kind: "personal"` refusal as it is (canonical form).

Run `cargo test -p cipherbox-core`, `cargo test --workspace --exclude fuser`, the release run of `encode_refusals`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy with `-D warnings`, the wasm32 check, `pnpm install`, the client unit and browser suites, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint:tracker-refs`. Regenerate the KAT vectors with `kat_gen`. Update the PR body through the REST API (`gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/1983 -F body=@file`) so it lists the re-mint carry, the budget, the deceptive-character rule and the new vectors; keep the three bare `Closes` lines and no attribution. Check `git log --format=%B origin/main..HEAD | grep -i "co-authored\|generated with"` prints nothing. Report the new head SHA, CI status, and the list of renamed or re-typed public items.

# #1969 engine: the claim carries the scope pointer name and re-posts until the deadline

The claim posts the scope pointer name with the contact code and the name. The engine re-posts the claim with one idempotency key until the deadline.

## Decisions

- [ADR 0023](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0023-the-invite-link-is-the-primary-sharing-path-and-conversion-runs-by-itself.md) D3, D6
- [ADR 0027](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0027-a-grantee-name-is-not-an-identity.md) D1

## Scope

- The claim payload is `{claimId, scopePointerName, contactCode, name}`.
- Each claim has one idempotency key. Every re-post uses the same key.
- Re-posts use exponential backoff. They stop at the deadline.
- A second claim of the same link on one device is a no-op. It is not a gate failure.
- The name is the sign-in display name by default. When there is no display name, the name is empty. The name is never the email.

## Acceptance

- Two posts of one claim carry one key.
- No post occurs after the deadline.
- A second claim command returns the existing state.
- Gate: the Rust gate (Workspace tests) blocks the merge.

## Files

- `crates/engine/src/grants/invite.rs` (claim)
- `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` claim command
- `crates/engine/src/api/client.rs`

## Batch

PR batch C with #1976 and #1970.

## Depends on

Part of #1963.

# #1970 engine: conversion runs on the tick and on dialog open, ack first

Any owner device converts claims on every tick and when the share dialog opens. The device acks the mailbox item first. It converts only when the API answers "removed". There is no approve step.

## Decisions

- [ADR 0023](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0023-the-invite-link-is-the-primary-sharing-path-and-conversion-runs-by-itself.md) D3, D4, D5, D6, D7, D9
- [ADR 0024](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0024-a-link-holder-reads-at-once-from-the-link-blob.md) D4
- [ADR 0026](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0026-a-scope-root-takes-many-grants.md) C5, E1
- [ADR 0027](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0027-a-grantee-name-is-not-an-identity.md) D3

## Scope

- On every tick and on share-dialog open, any owner device opens the claim items.
- The device acks first. It converts only when the API answers "removed".
- Run the D3 checks: the link entry is live; the kind is link; the deadline verdict; the contact code binding; the admission cap.
- The device computes the deadline verdict once, at the ack, against the injected `now`. It stores the verdict in the op entry.
- The admission cap counts the live rows that have the via-link reference. It does not count the owner.
- When the identity already has a row, conversion is a no-op. It never changes an existing row.
- Conversion appends the personal row at the conversion permission, with the via-link reference, the grantee name and the source `claimant`.
- For a write link, conversion mints the write material. When the folder has no write scope, it runs a write-scope cut first.
- The engine publishes one root per folder per tick.
- Conversion is a durable op entry. Its retry covers the full conversion.
- A refusal at the 1024-row cap dead-letters the entry. It does not block the queue.
- The engine never cuts a link that has a pending op entry.
- The converting device shows one transient "joined" notice.
- The people list updates on every owner device from the record.

## Acceptance

- A claim from device A converts on device B.
- A "not removed" answer converts nothing.
- A write conversion on a read-only folder runs one write-scope cut.
- A link with a full cap refuses the conversion.
- A second claim by the same identity appends no row.
- After a transient failure, the retry runs the checks again.
- Gate: the Rust gate (Workspace tests) blocks the merge.

## Files

- `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` `convert_invite_claims`
- `crates/engine/src/grants/invite.rs` convert
- `ops` queue
- `crates/engine/src/api/client.rs` mailbox DELETE

## Batch

PR batch C with #1976 and #1969.

## Depends on

Part of #1963.

# #1971 engine: a grant or a link on a shared folder appends a row
When a folder already names a scope, a direct grant and a link mint append a row to the ledger. They do not make a new seed. The owner can edit a grantee name.
## Decisions
- [ADR 0026](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0026-a-scope-root-takes-many-grants.md) D1-D7, C5
- [ADR 0027](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0027-a-grantee-name-is-not-an-identity.md) D4, D6
## Scope
- When the folder already names a scope, the direct grant and the link mint use the append path: append a row, sign again, publish once. There is no new seed and no re-seal of the subtree.
- Retire the `grant-target-already-names-a-scope` refusal for this case.
- A grant to an existing grantee with a different permission calls the permission change (E6). With the same permission, it answers already-has-access.
- A folder can have any number of live links.
- Nested scopes do not change.
- The owner edits a grantee name in the people list. This is a row update with source `owner` and one root publish.
- Each device keeps a contact-book cache of names by identity for pre-fill. The cache is never synced.
## Acceptance
- A second grant appends a row and publishes once.
- The retired refusal does not occur.
- A name edit changes only the name and the flag of that row.
- Gate: the Rust gate (Workspace tests) blocks the merge.
## Files
- `crates/engine/src/grants/create.rs`
- `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`
- `seams` (contact-book cache)
## Batch
PR batch D with #1972.
## Depends on
Part of #1963.
# #1972 engine: a grantee's permission can change
The owner can change the permission of a grantee. An upgrade mints write material. A downgrade is a write revoke that keeps the read row. The permission of a link does not change.
## Decisions
- [ADR 0025](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0025-revocation-under-the-link-first-model.md) D6
- [ADR 0026](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0026-a-scope-root-takes-many-grants.md) D4
## Scope
- An upgrade from read to write mints the write material. When the folder has no write scope, it runs a write-scope cut first.
- A downgrade from write to read is a write revoke. It keeps the read row.
- The permission of a link is fixed.
## Acceptance
- An upgrade on a read-only folder runs one write-scope cut, and the grantee can write.
- A downgrade runs the write cut, and the grantee can still read.
- Gate: the Rust gate (Workspace tests) blocks the merge.
## Files
- `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`
- `crates/engine/src/rotation/trigger.rs`
## Batch
PR batch D with #1971.
## Depends on
Part of #1963.

**Findings**

1. **should-fix**: `/shared` has no "from <name>", and the engine discards the verified owner name.

   - Where: `apps/web/src/hooks/useSharingActions.ts:106-107`.

Otherwise, let the owner type a name. Add this to #1978 or file it with a dependency edge.

3. **nit**: the three messages are not the ADR 0025 D5 words.
   - Where: `apps/web/src/sharing/receivedShares.ts:28,29,52`.
   - Defect:

     | --- | --- |
     | "The owner removed you" | 'the owner removed you from this folder' |
     | "The link expired" | 'this link expired' |
     | "The link was revoked" | 'the owner revoked this link' |

   - Failure: the words differ from the normative text. A later e2e that asserts the ADR text will fail.
   - Fix: use the ADR words in lowercase ('the owner removed you', 'the link expired', 'the link was revoked'), and change the three assertions in `SharedPage.test.tsx`.

   - Where: `packages/client/src/worker/commandCodec.ts:904`.

The slice follows ADR 0024 D5 in most points. I found 4 should-fix defects and 5 nits. The most important defect: the engine deletes `linkSecret` before the personal blob opens.

## Findings

1. **should-fix**: `crates/engine/src/grants/received_status.rs:475-478`
   - **Defect:** The engine drops the link keys when the pass classifies the share as `Granted`. It does not wait for the personal blob to open. The `open` call can fail (513-516 sets `Unresolvable`) or can skip the blob (496 scope not renderable, 881 own tree, 937 seam error). The drop still persists (573-591).
   - **Scenario:** A co-writer re-seal publishes a personal blob that fails the AEAD open. The holder deletes `linkSecret`, and it cannot read through the link or through the personal blob. ADR 0024 D2 says "the persist that records the first personal **open**".
   - **Fix:** Push `HoldChange::Drop` only after `open` returns `Ok(Some(_))` on the personal path.

2. **should-fix**: `received_status.rs:372-373` and `:589-591`, against `facade.rs:9062-9079`
   - **Defect:** The refresh is now a load-modify-persist writer of the received-shares list, and it spans many network awaits. The claim command writes the same list at the same time, and nothing locks the list.
   - **Scenario:**
     - The tick loads the list.
     - The user joins link B. The command persists B and its `linkSecret`.
     - The tick then persists its stale copy. The tick persists on every first read, heal or deadline change, so this is a normal pass.
     - B is lost. The claim is posted, but nothing reads until conversion.
   - **Fix:** Load the list again just before the persist and apply the heal, deadline and drop changes by key. Alternatively, serialize all writers of the list through one engine async lock.

3. **should-fix**: `received_status.rs:633`
   - **Defect:** When the pointer consult returns `Unavailable` or `Ok(None)`, the pass keeps the last healed root name. It then resolves and renders that name, which is not this pass's `currentRootName` (ADR 0024 D5 item 3).
   - **Scenario:** A relay hides the pointer after a write wave. The blueprint says the old name is "dead to survivors" and a revoked write grantee can take it over. A replayed pre-wave owner record at a higher IPNS sequence then renders stale content. The personal path has the same weakness.
   - **Fix:** On the link path, do not render (classify `Unresolvable`) unless this pass vouched the name. At least, measure the record against the write-epoch floor that the consult raised.

4. **should-fix**: `crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs:4319-4325`
   - **Defect:** No test covers this change. It copies the link terms (kind, deadline, conversion permission, admission cap) onto the entry that a write wave re-mints. The test `a_root_a_write_wave_moved_still_opens_through_the_pointer` mints the link directly at the current root and runs no real wave.

After a revoke, `held` at `invite.rs:879-893` is `None`, so a redelivered item gives `ClaimOutcome::Granted`.

If the link is live and before its deadline, the next "convert" re-grants the claimant. The new grant is a personal row with no deadline (see the `ConvertedClaim::row` doc), so it outlives the link.

**Files analyzed:** 14 focus files, plus the callers: `facade.rs` (claim and convert), `ledger.rs`, `create.rs`, `net/pointer_fetch.rs`, `core/payload/pointer.rs`.
**Crypto operations found:** 11. **Issues found:** 0 Critical, 0 High, 2 Medium, 3 Low, 3 Info.
**Risk level: MEDIUM.** The crypto primitives, the domain separation, the AAD binding and the KAT are correct. The two Medium findings are in the protocol, at conversion. The PR removes the owner's replay guards, and it does not add the replacement that ADR 0023 specifies.

### Executive summary

The invite-names preimage is correct and pinned by KATs. The retired kind 0x03 is refused on seal and on open in release builds. The link-held read opens and verifies the re-point object before it reads any record. All entropy comes through the seam. The conversion path has two gaps:

- The server can replay a claim that was already converted.
- The admission cap is signed into the commitment but no code checks it.

### Findings

#### [MEDIUM] M1: The server can replay a converted claim after a revoke. CONFIRMED (mechanism traced)

**Location:** `crates/engine/src/grants/invite.rs:829-911`, `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` (the loop in `convert_invite_claims`, about lines 9150-9260), `crates/engine/kat/checks/manifest.json` (`claim-already-converted` and `grant-was-cut` are removed).

**Issue:** On the base branch, `recorded_claim_link` refused a spent claim id, and `GrantWasCut` refused to re-grant a tag the owner had cut (base `invite.rs:825-830`). This PR removes both. The replacement in ADR 0023 is the D5 ack lock and the op-entry verdict, and this PR does not implement them. Conversion still converts first and acks second. After a revoke, `held` at `invite.rs:879-893` is `None`, so a redelivered item gives `ClaimOutcome::Granted`.

**Impact:** The mailbox server is untrusted. It can keep a sealed claim item and deliver it again after the owner revokes that claimant. If the link is live and before its deadline, the next "convert" re-grants the claimant. The new grant is a personal row with no deadline (see the `ConvertedClaim::row` doc), so it outlives the link.

The revoked device no longer holds the capability: `HoldChange::Drop` removed `linkSecret` at conversion (`received_status.rs:~470`). So the server alone restores access that the owner removed.

**Recommendation:** Land ADR 0023 D5 (ack first, verdict in the op entry) in the same stack before the spent set goes. If D5 cannot land first, keep a narrow guard and a reject vector that fails until it lands. Tell the ADR owner about one limit: even D5's "delete answered removed" is a server answer. The spec should state the residual, "a live link plus a server replay re-admits a revoked person", or the revoke flow should also cut the link that admitted the person.

**Impact:** The claim is HPKE base mode, and the only signature on it is the ephemeral key's. One holder of the URL can enrol any number of self-made contact codes, up to `MAX_GRANT_BLOBS` (1024). The owner's scope then fills (`GrantSetFull`), and each conversion re-signs and republishes the set. Conversion grants `read` only now, so there is no write escalation. The PR still states "admission cap … default 25", and that cap has no effect.

**Recommendation:** Write `viaLink` on the converted row. Count the live rows that carry that reference, and refuse at `admission_cap` with a release-active `Err` and a reject vector. Until then, do not show the cap in the share dialog.

- `post_invite_claim` sends the claimant's contact code to the forwarder.

S3. (link-read 2) The refresh is a load-modify-persist writer of the received-shares list across network awaits, and the claim command writes the same list. Load the list again just before the persist and apply the heal, deadline and drop changes by key (or serialize every writer through one engine async lock). Test: a join during a pass is not lost.
S4. (link-read 3) On the link path never render a record under a root name this pass did not vouch through the pointer. When the consult is unavailable, keep the previous classification and render nothing new; when the pointer is absent (`Ok(None)`), classify Unresolvable. Test: a pointer that goes unavailable after a wave does not render the old root.
S5. (link-read 4 + spec) Add an `owner_actions` test: mint a link, join, run a REAL write wave, the holder is still `Granted`, the entry is still a link with the same deadline, and the holder reads through the moved root.
S6. (crypto L3) `MalformedFragment` gets the class `malformed`, the same as a malformed claim.
S7. (crypto L1) Add accept KAT vectors that pin the fragment bytes (the claim vector belongs to the claim slice). Add a release-run encode refusal for an oversize contact code in the fragment (2048-byte bound).
S8. (standards silent fallback) `received_status.rs:717` `EphemeralInvitee::from_secret(..).ok()` drops an invalid stored secret silently. Classify that share Unresolvable and emit nothing else; do not skip it silently.
S9. (crypto M1, M2 — state, do not build) The spent set is gone, so the mailbox server can replay a converted claim after a revoke until ack-first lands, and the admission cap is signed but not enforced until conversion writes `viaLink` rows. Both are the claim/conversion slice, which lands next in this stack. State both windows in the PR body under "Known windows closed by the next slice". P1. `facade.rs:559` `invite_links: Option<SharingInviteLinks>` is always `Some`: make it non-optional through wasm (`invite_links` getter), `protocol.ts:263`, `sharing.store.ts:47`, `commandCodec.ts:933`; delete the web `unavailable` state (`inviteLink.ts:57-63`, `InviteLinkPanel.tsx:38`), `NoLocalLink` (`InviteLinkPanel.tsx:123-131`, its text is false now) and their tests. P2. One expiry predicate at one home: `UnixMillis::reached(self, deadline: Option<UnixMillis>) -> bool` (or `deadline_passed`) used by `LinkHold::is_expired`, `CommittedLink::is_expired`, `received_status.rs:761` and `rotation/trigger.rs:627`. Decide the `Expired` class once in the refresh loop after `classified` (a fresh deadline read this pass wins over the stored one); `Classified::unresolvable` takes no parameters.
P3. `received_status.rs:283` replace `link_deadline: Option<Option<UnixMillis>>` with `hold_change: Option<HoldChange>` computed at the tail of `classified`; the caller does `hold_changes.extend(hold_change)`. P4. P5. `rotation/trigger.rs:616-627` `prune_expired_grants` keeps a vestigial `owner_deadlines` parameter and has no production caller: delete the function and its tests (the sweep slice adds what it needs), or, if a production caller exists, remove the parameter and read `entry.deadline`.
P6. `invite.rs:507-531` `from_tree` and `accept.rs:614-617` `read_link_hold`: replace the hand wipe with `Zeroizing` and `?`.
P7. `accept.rs:229-237` delete the hand-written `Debug` for `LinkHold`; derive it (`SecretBytes` already redacts).
P8. `accept.rs:594-605` write the pair check as two `if`s and the deadline as `.map(..).transpose()?`.
P9. `facade.rs:9070` call `received.find(&key)` once; build `pending_link_bookmark` only when it is used (efficiency 3).
P10. `link_read.rs:34,55` store `""` as the display name when the names do not verify; the host renders "shared via link" when `viaLink && displayName === ''`. Add the test for the fallback at join.
P11. Keep `CommittedLink::conversion_permission` (the conversion slice reads it). Say so in one commit line, not in a comment.

## Reuse (apply)
R1. `sole_link(links) -> Option<&CommittedLink>` in `invite.rs`, used by `locate_invite_link` and the sharing read at `facade.rs:10689-10694` (delete the comment that says the rule is repeated).
R2. `block_on_while_ticking` in `testkit/executor.rs` exported from `testkit/mod.rs`; use it in `owner_actions.rs`, delete the local `command_while_ticking`.
R3. `invite_mint.rs:139` and `testkit/checks.rs:549`: use `cipherbox_core::suite::ecdsa::SIGNATURE_LEN` / `ECDSA_SIG_LEN`, not `64`.
R4. `invite_mint.rs:666-671` test: use `grants::self_locate_signed`.

## Efficiency (apply)
E1. `received_status.rs:610` `follow_held_pointers` shares `MAX_RESOLVES_PER_PASS` with the main loop, in the same list order (a forced pass otherwise resolves up to 1024 pointers).
E2. `facade.rs:9081` `claim_invite_link` files the forced pass without waiting on `pass.landed()`; the bookmark is already durable. Confirm that dropping the `ForcedPass` handle still runs the pass (`refresh.rs:129`). The host shows "claimed" before the listing updates; that is acceptable.
E3. (low) `convert_invite_claims` computes `committed_links` N+1 times; pass the list into `convert_invite_claim` and keep `authorise` per item. Optional; skip if the conversion slice rewrites the loop.

## Standards (apply)
T1. Absence-justifying comment at `invite.rs:824-825` ("A write grant needs the write material and a write-scope cut that this function does not run."): delete.
T2. The rule "a link entry is committed at read, no write-scope cut (ADR 0024 D4)" is stated at `invite.rs:14-16`, `invite.rs:287-288`, `invite_mint.rs:10-11`, `facade.rs:1191-1192`, `facade.rs:8441-8442`, `received_status.rs:490`: keep ONE citation at the mint, delete the rest. The ADR 0025 D5 `viaLink` note at `facade.rs:610`, `lib.rs:1226`, `protocol.ts:307`, `receivedShares.ts:49`: keep the Rust one and the TS type one.
T3. "fragment holder" → "link holder" at `invite.rs:610` and `invite.rs:718`. `facade.rs:8480` narration comment: delete.
T4. `packages/client/src/facade.ts:378`: `expiresAt?: bigint`, `ownerName = ''`; `useSharingActions.ts:107` passes no name; the comment cites ADR 0027 D5 (owner name in the fragment, source unstated) and says the D1 never-email rule applies by analogy. Keep the note once, at the facade default.

## Tests missing (add)
M1. A first read that fails and a later tick read that succeeds. M2. A facade-level join of an expired link. M3. A join of the same link twice on one device keeps the stored deadline (link-read nit 7).

## Run
`cargo test -p cipherbox-core`, `cargo test -p cipherbox-engine`, `cargo test --workspace --exclude fuser --exclude cipherbox-desktop`, both `kat_gen` runs with no drift, `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy `-D warnings`, the wasm32 check, `pnpm install`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, the `packages/client` and `apps/web` unit tests, `pnpm lint:tracker-refs`. Update the PR body through the REST API: the changes, the tests and gates, the "Known windows closed by the next slice" section, the bookmark-key deviation, the two `Closes` lines, no attribution. Check `git log --format=%B origin/feat/1963-core-link-fields..HEAD | grep -i "co-authored\|generated with"` prints nothing. Report the new head SHA and every renamed or re-typed public item (lanes E and F build on your branch).

entries.name: CronCreate
entries.description:
Schedule a prompt to be enqueued at a future time. Use for both recurring schedules and one-shot reminders.

Uses standard 5-field cron in the user's local timezone: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. "0 9 * * *" means 9am local — no timezone conversion needed.

## One-shot tasks (recurring: false)

For "remind me at X" or "at <time>, do Y" requests — fire once then auto-delete.
Pin minute/hour/day-of-month/month to specific values:
  "remind me at 2:30pm today to check the deploy" → cron: "30 14 <today_dom> <today_month> *", recurring: false
  "tomorrow morning, run the smoke test" → cron: "57 8 <tomorrow_dom> <tomorrow_month> *", recurring: false

## Recurring jobs (recurring: true, the default)

For "every N minutes" / "every hour" / "weekdays at 9am" requests:
  "*/5 * * * *" (every 5 min), "0 * * * *" (hourly), "0 9 * * 1-5" (weekdays at 9am local)

## Avoid the :00 and :30 minute marks when the task allows it

Every user who asks for "9am" gets `0 9`, and every user who asks for "hourly" gets `0 *` — which means requests from across the planet land on the API at the same instant. When the user's request is approximate, pick a minute that is NOT 0 or 30:
  "every morning around 9" → "57 8 * * *" or "3 9 * * *" (not "0 9 * * *")
  "hourly" → "7 * * * *" (not "0 * * * *")
  "in an hour or so, remind me to..." → pick whatever minute you land on, don't round

Only use minute 0 or 30 when the user names that exact time and clearly means it ("at 9:00 sharp", "at half past", coordinating with a meeting). When in doubt, nudge a few minutes early or late — the user will not notice, and the fleet will.

## Session-only

Jobs live only in this Claude session — nothing is written to disk, and the job is gone when Claude exits.

## Not for live watching

CronCreate re-runs a prompt at fixed wall-clock intervals. To watch a log file, process, or command output and be notified the moment something changes, use the Monitor tool instead — Monitor streams events as they happen; cron polls on a schedule.

## Runtime behavior

Jobs only fire while the REPL is idle (not mid-query). The scheduler adds a small deterministic jitter on top of whatever you pick: recurring tasks fire up to 10% of their period late (max 15 min); one-shot tasks landing on :00 or :30 fire up to 90 s early. Picking an off-minute is still the bigger lever.

Recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days — they fire one final time, then are deleted. This bounds session lifetime. Tell the user about the 7-day limit when scheduling recurring jobs.

Returns a job ID you can pass to CronDelete.

cron.description: Standard 5-field cron expression in local time: "M H DoM Mon DoW" (e.g. "*/5 * * * *" = every 5 minutes, "30 14 28 2 *" = Feb 28 at 2:30pm local once).

prompt.description: The prompt to enqueue at each fire time.

recurring.description: true (default) = fire on every cron match until deleted or auto-expired after 7 days. false = fire once at the next match, then auto-delete. Use false for "remind me at X" one-shot requests with pinned minute/hour/dom/month.

durable.description: Has no effect — durable persistence is not available. All jobs are session-only (in-memory, gone when this Claude session ends).

entries.name: CronDelete
entries.description: Cancel a cron job previously scheduled with CronCreate. Removes it from the in-memory session store.

entries.name: CronList
entries.description: List all cron jobs scheduled via CronCreate in this session.
